# Complementary raster initializer workaround R1

2026-10-08 · `/root/raster_initializer_fix` · **One new algorithm-preserving
source candidate staged; eight static tests pass. Apple compilation, rendering,
quality and GPU performance remain unverified.** Root owns all integration,
builds, client, reloads and GPU measurements. This worker edited only its new
ignored staging directory and this new report. No live process remains owned.

## Distinct premise and exact counterexample

Both prior fixed .75 sources reached Apple M3 `glLinkProgram` failures. The
sampler-forwarding workaround did not solve the boundary. Its actual R4 fragment
is [`001_deferred1.fsh`](../../run-workloads/cross-shader-performance-r1/complementary-raster-activation-r4/client/patched_shaders/001_deferred1.fsh),
SHA-256 `b3c76e99ba78c038d218e49414534bc31140c4fd1fde49d16339f7ebcde7f38a`;
vertex SHA-256 is
`16ba2b0bd352b0447bf89e4ecd3354ec23fc815241e8d59a2f4a401ca1cfe9bf`.
The fresh crash is [`hs_err_pid72582.log`](../../run-workloads/cross-shader-performance-r1/complementary-raster-activation-r4/client/hs_err_pid72582.log),
SHA-256 `f2ab589c274235b0786c78e8bd02e361278daf902d9f5dca49dd3662f03ba2c5`.
It repeats `glpLLVMGetFunctionGlobalVariableUse` before
`glpLLVMCGFindSamplersAndBuffers` and `glLinkProgram`. The inherited 15081 crash
remains separate; it is not new R4 evidence.

At actual fragment line 683, the original uniform-dependent global initializer
now reads:

```glsl
vec2 view = vec2((shaderlodRasterR1Scene().x), (shaderlodRasterR1Scene().y));
```

Its introduced user-function graph is `view → Scene → Size → On`, plus
`Scene → Output`; On reads the bridge/activation uniforms and Output reads native
width/height uniforms. This is a concrete compiler-sensitive source difference.
The crash stack does **not** establish that this initializer caused the driver
defect. All helper functions remain acyclic by the unchanged source; Apple
analysis behavior is unknown. No unchanged driver retry was made by this worker.

## One frozen helper-only change

[`helper.diff`](../../dev/logs/cross-shader-performance-r1/raster-initializer-fix/helper.diff)
changes only the final `viewWidth`/`viewHeight` object macros in archive member
`shaders/lib/shaderlod/raster_r1.glsl`, relative to sampler workaround
`286d9a565028cee58e19109e4172ce057ca5d6162a51c6a219c3c4f75fe11310`.
Each dimension expands into the same activation predicate and componentwise
`max(floor(nativeDimension * .75), 1.0)` or the native dimension. The identical
compile-time guard controls expansion; rejected guards retain raw uniform names.
The global initializer consequently calls only constructors and built-in
floor/max, with no introduced user-function call.

The macros deliberately reference their own uniform token. Standard object-macro
self-expansion suppression leaves that token as the raw native uniform; actual
glslang preprocessing verifies this for all 76 world0 stages. Width expansion
never refers to height, or conversely. No parameterized macro argument is added
or repeated. Two reads of each native uniform are pure and have no side effects.
The runtime predicate has exactly the tokens in the unchanged On function.
The scalar expression is the componentwise identity of the prior vec2 expression.
There is no altered arithmetic order within either component, approximation,
preset, scene, threshold, native option, or scale rescue.

All original helper function bodies, all sampling macros and their existing call
arguments, UV/key/history/filter/mip/resource/producer program bodies and native
AA are byte-identical to the previous candidate. No sampler signature, derivative,
sampling branch or resource property is changed. Active sampling retains prior
explicit LOD/affine bloom gradients; native sampling retains its prior fallback.
This change adds no new derivative control and no work behind a late branch.
Ordinary scalar helper calls inside function bodies intentionally remain, so
this candidate tests the global-initializer premise separately.

The side fraction remains **0.75, dimensionless**; allocation and output sizes
are pixel counts, with axis extents clamped to at least one pixel. There is no
distance band. Renderer-owned frame switching and history epoch reset remain
the required transition behavior; no smooth scale interpolation is introduced.
Original archive is the disabled baseline for Off/Quality, missing/unknown
bridge, unknown native option map, native TAA off or incomplete contract. DH,
VOXY, non-Overworld and shadow scopes retain native fallback. These are source
contracts; actual mod linkage and renderer restoration are separate runtime gates.

renderer contract. Verify actual newly exported deferred1 global `view` contains
pure uniform expressions and no ShaderLOD user-function calls. All original
function/sampling/resource fingerprints must remain intact. Effective uniforms,
not config bytes, must establish activation. If the same Apple link crash
recurs, save fresh fatal/export pins, stop that exact client and retire this
initializer hypothesis without a same-input retry or settings rescue.

If this candidate fails unchanged, the next distinct source premise is the
remaining scalar helper call graph inside ordinary function bodies. A bounded

while retaining Output as the raw-width/height function defined before dimension
macros; this tests nested helper analysis separately and avoids accidentally

# Complementary native water motion controls

This is bounded original-pack quality work, not a ShaderLOD adapter. Root has
rendered the pinned Complementary Reimagined r5.9.3 at native 2976×1672 with the
minimal Iris/Sodium stack, no DH and no main mod. The reported full/sky/Potato
pilot GPU means were 13.7679/12.3120/12.3002 ms. Root observed lost reflected trees
in sky-only and shifted projected geometry in Potato. Those tradeoffs have not
been accepted as adapter quality or a performance/support result.

This preparer creates fresh unchanged-release arms and a shared immutable
20-second **2 FPS / 41-frame** request. It does not launch, build, compile, encode
or change the source scene. Root owns real preparation, all clients/GPU and
actual image review. Lower sampling rate limits temporal conclusions: these
native sampled frames can expose moving reflection displacement, but cannot
exclude shimmer/flicker above 1 Hz or replace broader quality checks.

## Three serial native quality runs

benchmark mode. These exact commands physically exclude the main mod through
`runClientLodOff`, select minimal/noDH and the native scale2 window, and keep
GPU timing off. Never run the three windows concurrently. If source dev classes
need a build, root performs it before any client and rechecks artifact identity;
the following commands explicitly avoid recompiling dev classes during runs.

```sh
./gradlew --offline runClientLodOff -x compileDevClientJava -PrunDirectory="$PWD/run-workloads/complementary-motion-quality-r1/coastalwater/high" -PincludeDh=false -PperformanceStack=minimal -PbenchmarkWindowScale=2 -PgpuTiming=false -PfixedWetness=0 -PcameraQuality="$PWD/run-workloads/complementary-motion-quality-r1/camera-request.json" -PcameraQualityOnly=true
```

## Structural validation before image review

Choose the **explicit UUID manifest from the owned launch**; the validator does
not select a latest/first directory or pool old runs. Replace the UUID tokens:

```sh
python3 scripts/prepare_complementary_quality_profiles.py validate --output run-workloads/complementary-motion-quality-r1 --arm high --manifest run-workloads/complementary-motion-quality-r1/coastalwater/high/camera-quality/HIGH_UUID/manifest.json
python3 scripts/prepare_complementary_quality_profiles.py validate --output run-workloads/complementary-motion-quality-r1 --arm water-sky --manifest run-workloads/complementary-motion-quality-r1/coastalwater/water-sky/camera-quality/SKY_UUID/manifest.json
python3 scripts/prepare_complementary_quality_profiles.py validate --output run-workloads/complementary-motion-quality-r1 --arm water-potato --manifest run-workloads/complementary-motion-quality-r1/coastalwater/water-potato/camera-quality/POTATO_UUID/manifest.json
```

The readonly validator requires complete status, all41 unique ordered slots and
callbacks, zero skips, no pending image/callback leases, selected one-image bound,
unchanged request/control/artifacts, original archive hash, loaded native options
at every boundary, main/DH/optional-stack absence and dev/Iris/Sodium provenance.
Requested/effective detailed radius must be24 and all recorded framebuffers and
actual PNG IHDRs2976×1672/RGBA8. Every on-disk PNG hash/size and IHDR CRC is checked;
full raster decoding is left to root's image review and the tested writer.

All frames must have known NONE/no-full-collision/first-person camera contexts,
loaded actual chunk-cache guards and finite near-plane positions. The player
must stay500.5/68/660.5, rendered X/Z within0.0002 blocks, stable eyeY about69.62,
advancing source render frames and finite Iris clocks. Recorded path time must
stay within0.1 seconds of its half-second slot, and rendered yaw/pitch within
0.05 degrees of the current motion tick’s bounded eased request. LocalPlayer
rotation uses the current tick, while recorded path time/position use the partial
tick; the validator checks both clocks independently. Context and screenshot camera values
must agree. These checks do not prove glint/ray visibility, partial-shape
clearance, continuous fluid state between samples or visual parity.

Root then compares near/mid/far water and reflected bank/tree features through
the sweep. Inspect projected feature shift, screen-edge loss, depth intersections,
glint movement and temporal stability; align actual recorded cameras/path times
and account for advancing histories rather than assume identical pixel phase.
Sky-only's reflected-tree loss and Potato's projected displacement are native
tradeoffs to judge honestly. PNG capture overhead is unmeasured quality work;
do not derive a GPU optimization or adapter support from these sequences.

# Unbound native copy activation contract correction R6

2026-10-08 · `/root/unbound_temporal_activation` · **Staged observer expectation
correction only; fresh driver result pending.** No shader/controller/release pin,
active source, build, client, GPU, Goal or STATUS changed. Initial failures and
R1–R5 evidence remain preserved. Parent exclusively owns integration and runtime.
Only ignored `activation/copy-contract-r6/` and this new report were written.

The [actual failed R5 report](../../dev/logs/cross-shader-performance-r2/unbound-temporal-runtime-r5/candidate/activation.json)
reached composite3 with controller active, viewport/scissor 1440 × 900, native
WORLD_BLUR=0 and all four activation uniform locations -1. It correctly retained
`all_linked_activation_predicates_true=false`, then failed the blanket consuming
uniform requirement before c3 FBO/sampler observations. This is a nonconsuming

# Reimagined nonmip sampler rule R1

**CONDITIONAL_SOURCE_ROUTE; CURRENT_RUNTIME_GATE_PENDING.** Nonuniform implicit-call syntax alone does not establish that the entire lookup is undefined under the stated nonmip, equal-filter, isotropic states. It also does not establish current-driver equivalence, finite outputs, or permission to force a new LOD. Parent owns admission; the existing stopped source stages remain unchanged.

## Primary specification answer

[GLSL 4.00 revision9 §8.9, printed pp116–120](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/GLSLangSpec.4.00.pdf#page=122) states: “Implicit derivatives are undefined within non-uniform control flow”. That is a derivative rule, not an unconditional whole-lookup rule. It separately uses a nonmip texture directly. §8.9.2 defines textureLod with explicit λbase and zero partial derivatives. §3.8.2 includes lane-specific breaks and partial loop iterations as nonuniform flow. Inference: a result independent of those undefined inputs need not become undefined solely because of control flow. This inference assumes finite valid texture coordinates and a valid sampler/texture pairing; it does not bless NaN coordinates or prove driver intermediate finiteness.

[OpenGL4.1 core §3.8.11–12, printed pp225–235](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/glspec41.core.pdf#page=241) specifies base-level LINEAR filtering, with magnification LINEAR behaving identically to minification LINEAR. Consequently ordinary color filtering at identical coordinates has no mip/filter-selection dependence under these states. But [§3.8.16, printed p239](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/glspec41.core.pdf#page=255) permits implementation-dependent multi-depth comparison for LINEAR. Its wording includes: “The details of this are implementation-dependent”. This supports preserving native hardware PCF, not claiming a portable exact PCF footprint. §3.9.2 also requires matching shadow sampler type, depth format and comparison mode. Base-level identity, completeness and absence of framebuffer feedback remain prerequisites.

[ARB_shader_texture_lod revision11, Overview](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/extensions/ARB/ARB_shader_texture_lod.txt) explicitly connects undefined texels in divergent flow to mipmap and anisotropic fetches. This corroborates the limited derivative interpretation; it supplies no additional guarantee that native and explicit-LOD shadow instructions agree on this driver. [ARB_texture_filter_anisotropic, additions to minification/magnification](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/extensions/ARB/ARB_texture_filter_anisotropic.txt) defines maxAniso1 as isotropic. This later ARB text is corroboration, not evidence that Apple's GL4.1 advertises that extension; the historical receipt reports anisotropy support without enumerating its extension spelling.

**Practical result:** unchanged native implicit reads under an additional representative branch are a viable *conditional* source route if their effective current states remove every derivative-consuming sampling feature. Ordinary nonmip/isotropic color sampling meets the mathematical filter argument. Shadow comparison retains a driver-specific PCF boundary; no exact hardware footprint or bitwise parity is certified. Native divergent loops are not proof for a new branch: compiler scheduling, active lanes and instruction lowering may change, and historical images do not expose these intermediates.

textureLod0 would select the same base image and ordinary LINEAR color filter under these prerequisites, rather than necessarily creating a different color footprint. Nevertheless it changes λbase/derivative inputs; shadow PCF parity is not proven. A matched full-work control only proves parity to that changed kernel, not original Photon/Reimagined. The assignment forbids forced LOD for parity, so **do not introduce textureLod0, sampler changes, fixed gradients or policy retuning**. If the driver-specific boundary cannot be accepted and verified within existing authorized hooks, retain STOP.

# Complementary HALF VL sample phase correction R4

2026-10-07; bounded shader worker `vl_sample_phase_fix`. Static-only handback
for the existing R4 setup/screen deadlines; no extension or runtime ownership.

## Derivation and change

Pinned Complementary Reimagined r5.9.3 original archive SHA256
`fed6c879e732cf7fc7bc6570ebb1def43235aa7e96f62859fbdbdbfa0b484b38`;
upstream EminGT attribution and License.txt retained byte-for-byte.

For the supported even native viewport, `view = 2 * grid`. Reduced cell `c`
rasterizes at `shaderlodGridUV = (c + 0.5) / grid`. The unchanged producer
selects native integer pixel `floor(shaderlodGridUV * view) = 2*c + 1`, then
uses native pixel-center UV `(2*c + 1.5) / view`. The old resolver's
`q = texCoord * grid - 0.5` evaluates to `c + 0.25` at that actual sample.
Invert the producer's lattice with `q = (texCoord * view - 1.5) * 0.5`;
equivalently `texCoord * grid - 0.75`. Only this expression and its comments
change. Cell clamping, four-tap interpolation and sample-transmission lookup
remain unchanged. Coordinates are native pixels/reduced cells; existing depth
rejection remains in blocks through `GetLinearDepth(z) * far`.

No change to native integration/kernel/ray counts, transmission, rejection,
factor feedback, scene, TAA or outputs. The nearest-surface fallback remains
when no compatible weighted tap exists; silhouette blur remains a quality risk.
No new transition or quality tuning. `SHADERLOD_VL_RATE=0` still disables the
prepass and selects the original native full-resolution integration at compile
time; resolver is guarded by `SHADERLOD_VL_RATE==1 && OVERWORLD`. Native AA and
quality remain selected upstream. Switching requires reload and history reset.
Odd viewport and resizing remain unsupported/unverified by this private pilot;
this correction assumes the runtime gate's fixed 1920 × 1200 / 960 × 600 sizes.

Entry points: `shaders/world0/composite1.{fsh,vsh}` include producer
`shaders/program/shaderlod_vl_rate.glsl`; full-native
`shaders/world0/composite2.{fsh,vsh}` include original `composite1.glsl`, whose
On branch calls `ShaderLODResolveVL` from
`shaders/lib/shaderlod/vl_rate_resolve.glsl`. Sampling remains integer
`texelFetch(..., 0)` without derivative-dependent fetches or late hidden work.

# Unbound temporal format syntax repair R4

2026-10-08 · `/root/unbound_temporal_shader` · **Two-directive source repair;
actual driver/resource admission still pending.** Parent reported R3 advanced

`const int colortex10Format=RGBA8` in deferred2 and
`const int colortex9Format=R11F_G11F_B10F` in composite2. Those names are Iris

```glsl
const int colortex10Format = RGBA8;
```

records.text:
# Unbound depth renderer R2 independent review

**ADMIT one finite untimed driver trial.** No decisive source counterexample was found in the frozen renderer stage. This admits integration/driver investigation only: it establishes no successful Mixin application, coverage equality, visual quality, avoided fragment work or performance gain. Parent owns integration, build and the sole client/GPU lane. Review is terminal with no live jobs.

Reviewed the current goal contract, renderer report, all seven staged Java files, bootstrap/build patch, shader ABI and exact pinned Iris/Sodium class bytes. Independently generated `javap -c -p` artifacts from those jars under [review-renderer](../../dev/logs/cross-shader-performance-r2/unbound-depth-priming-r2/review-renderer/). No project build, client, GL context or GPU measurement was launched by this reviewer.

## Frozen provenance and bootstrap

[Independent pin receipt](../../dev/logs/cross-shader-performance-r2/unbound-depth-priming-r2/review-renderer/pin-check.json) verifies both jar hashes, all 23 listed class hashes, all 12 staged postimages, integration patch, frozen report and source ABI hashes. At first inspection active build.gradle/mods.toml already differed from old preimages because the parent had integrated the patch; all 12 active postimages now independently match the frozen stage. The preserved ComplementaryRasterR1 preimage still matches. This is expected parent integration, not an invalid freeze.

The private source set has main APIs/output and pinned local Iris/Sodium dependencies. Its mod metadata registers the required client mixin config; false flag short-circuits before API inspection/injected renderer execution. The plugin checks raw class resources. Whether NeoForge supplies those exact resources and applies every shadow/accessor/injection is a driver launch gate. A silent false gate/native fallback is not candidate admission. Main production packaging, other versions/loaders and DH are outside this dev-only stage.

The `@Unique final EnumMap` initializer is not expected to wait until SodiumPrograms constructor return. In locally cached sponge-mixin 0.15.2 + Mixin 0.8.7, `Initialiser.injectInto` uses `Constructor.findInitialiserInjectionPoint`: SAFE chooses the delegate/super constructor; DEFAULT advances only to writes of mixin-initialized fields. Native SodiumPrograms has no write to the new shaderlod$depth field, so its anchor remains Object constructor invocation at bytecode 1, before createShader at 184. Raw [constructor algorithm](../../dev/logs/cross-shader-performance-r2/unbound-depth-priming-r2/review-renderer/Constructor.javap.txt) and [initializer insertion](../../dev/logs/cross-shader-performance-r2/unbound-depth-priming-r2/review-renderer/Initialiser.javap.txt) support availability during shader construction. Actual transformed class application is unobserved.

## Replay and mixed-pass semantics

Native DefaultChunkRenderer render bytecode 53 sets model-view, 58–69 creates the region iterator, then calls fillCommandBuffer → ensureCapacity → prepareTessellation → region-offset setter → executeDrawBatch. The injection sits between matrices and that iterator. SOLID/CUTOUT are both non-translucent in the pinned DefaultTerrainRenderPasses, so candidate iterator(false), shared unsigned-int indices and ordinary tessellation exactly select the native path. Native fillCommandBuffer clears batch on every region and obtains a fresh section iterator; ImmediateDrawCommandList submits the arrays immediately through nglMultiDrawElementsBaseVertex. Native executeDrawBatch closes its tessellation scope even on failure. No new list/batch pointer is retained across regions/frames, and no visibility/upload/sprite/task traversal is replayed.

The native colour loop remains intact and starts its own iterator after the prepass. This does not globally prime CUTOUT before SOLID colour: each ordinary native pass receives only its own priming loop. Snow is absent from priming but still included in native colour; a nearer snow surface can pass LEQUAL against a farther primed surface. Equal-depth colour ownership remains native order with blending excluded. Actual raster/coverage equality and derivative-sensitive surviving shading still require driver/quality checks.

## Program inputs and state restoration

Pinned SodiumPrograms constructs compiled stage objects before createShader; its HEAD hook receives those actual objects before native builder/link and before stage deletion. The hook inspects their actual glGetShaderSource declarations, requires GLSL330/invariant position and matching invariant texCoord/flat-int mat interfaces, then attaches that same native vertex object to the coverage builder. Calling native buildProgram retains every native attribute binding and constructs SodiumShader with the same pipeline, pass, source directives, alpha reference, custom uniforms and flip supplier. Native colour construction then proceeds. The declaration guard is admission inspection; it is neither a full GLSL equivalence proof nor an observed transformed-source receipt.

SodiumShader setup populates common/custom uniforms, images/samplers and atlas shrink; candidate then sets the same projection/model-view and native region/camera offsets. The selected vertex and coverage code use no additional texture operations beyond atlas coverage, while native bindTextures touches units 0 and 2. The actual driver must still establish the selected atlas/filter/alpha and live vertex inputs. IDs in an admission message alone do not establish those values.

State.capture checks the actual native program/FBO/depth object, LEQUAL, depth test/write, every indexed writable MRT mask and every indexed disabled blend; unsupported stencil/offset/sample/discard modes reject. Native pack properties have no terrain blend directive, and both terrain pass objects are non-translucent. Actual native GL state, rather than those source labels, remains decisive. Priming changes only colour masks; restoring all-true before callback/cache setters is valid because capture/begin require all masks true. Depth function/mask are untouched.

Pinned SodiumShader.resetState really clears uniform tracking, clears/unbinds all sampler tracking and binds Minecraft main target. The finally chain correctly rebinds/setup-populates native program before explicitly rebinding owning terrain framebuffer and restoring separate draw/read FBOs, atlas/lightmap bindings, samplers, active texture and raster state through native cache owners. Other native sampler bindings are repopulated by native setup after clear. Native matrices live in their own program and are not overwritten by coverage matrices. The first pass assertion checks actual restored state, but no GL restoration has been observed here.

Successful coverage programs are deleted at pipeline destroy HEAD. Coverage fragment deletion and explicit builder-program cleanup cover build/link/interface failures after allocation. Upstream GlShader compilation failure has no internal cleanup, and a createShader HEAD failure can precede native stage cleanup; a partly constructed pipeline can also retain programs. These are bounded trial failure limitations: stop the owned client process on construction/link failure rather than reload/retry inside it. They preclude production lifetime acceptance, not one finite process trial.

## Finding and next decisive gate

**P2 evidence limitation — empty-pass receipt can consume admission.** DepthChunkRendererMixin increments `draws` only when a nonempty region executes, but calls admission even when draws = 0; DepthPrimingR2 then remembers the pass until pack identity changes. Reproduction from source: an eligible empty SOLID/CUTOUT iterator produces a first `SHADERLOD_DEPTH_R2_ADMISSION draws=0`, and subsequent populated frames emit no replacement receipt. A trial must obtain both pass receipts with positive draw counts, otherwise this is missing execution evidence, not acceptance. No source change was assigned to this reviewer.

Allow the parent's already bounded driver trial only with the exact invariant archive/native398 and original/control/candidate distinctions. Require actual successful coverage links/Mixin application, both positive-draw pass receipts, native compatible state/restoration and ordinary-detail/foliage/water comparison against untouched original and invariant native-colour control. Incompatible depth/blend, native fallback, absent/zero receipts or conspicuous quality change stops this fixed trial; do not change settings/state to rescue it.

Candidate pays a full additional command-assembly/draw/vertex/alpha pass, repeated shader setup/reset/repopulation, per-pass State plus arrays and GL state queries, and a per-frame 398-option TreeMap comparison. All are real candidate costs; none may be removed from the later query-free original-relative cost screen. Opaque+cutout mean 1.5236 ms is only the previously observed eligible domain, not a total-frame saving or a throughput denominator. No speed claim is made. Driver behaviour, quality, useful total-frame benefit, normal UI restoration, DH/PBR and ports remain unverified.

# Reimagined literal AO independent source review

October16,2026. **Accept as a bounded source/math candidate. No blocking
coordinate, count, normalization or supported-fallback defect found.** Rendering,
linked consumption, floating-point/image equivalence, motion quality and speed
remain unverified. Parent owns exact depth-source integration, build/client/GPU,
acceptance and restoration. Reviewer wrote only this report; no live process.

The change is a distinct compiler-specialization experiment after the negative
R40 dynamic-budget result. It does not establish that M3 unrolling caused that
result or that literal kernels run faster.

## Exact authentic inputs and assembly

Public-selection versus private-builder metadata/note filenames differ; these

## Count, near and kernel equivalence

The exact supported dispatch guard retains master1, IS_IRIS, MC12101,
IRIS10812, Overworld, !DH, !VOXY and adds SSAO_QUALI2 for literal specialization.
Outside it, the old generic loop remains. Native quality3's12-sample path is not
specialized; no other loader/version or stale reader receives a support claim.

The R40 selector text is unchanged: native sample declaration, native z0<.56
early return, active AO flag and receiverDistance>shaderlodNear, then existing
refinement budget with minimum2. The ordinary caller still passes
length(viewPos.xyz), not homogeneous vec4 length or normalized depth.
For native4, current valid retained ratios .75..1 and ceil/clamp produce only3
or4; invalid bridge/core/preset/bands/distance return4. <=near retains4,
Balanced retains4, far Performance/AGGRESSIVE selects3, Quality/Off retains4.
The existing seven-argument reconstruction wrapper passes distance-1, keeping
native count. The excluded VOXY native call/signature remains present.

Each literal body equals the actual R40 body after removal of the unchanged
selector and native count/scm declaration, fixing scm=.4 and substituting count
3 or4 everywhere. This equality includes both depth queries, their order,
conditional AO-depth arithmetic/reuse logic, range clamps, index parity, native
radius/scale, accumulation order, normalization and final power. The three body
uses loop1..3, OffsetDist denominator3 and ao/=3; it is not first3-of4. Four uses

## Frozen algorithm and transition

Scale is a dimensionless side fraction, not a distance band. Camera translation
and reconstructed view depth are Minecraft blocks; sample positions are internal
pixels, velocity output pixels, coordinates normalized logical UV.

For output center `u`, current displacement `delta`, internal extent `I`,
`key=(u+delta)*I-.5`. Center is nearest valid key; its unjittered sample is
`s=(center+.5)/I-delta`. Total displacement is
`delta=(phase+.5*nativeJitterOffset*amplitude)/I`; four phases are
`(-.25,-.25),(.25,-.25),(.25,.25),(-.25,.25)` internal pixels. Native amplitude
is .125/.33/1 for jitter1/2/3. `TAAJitter(coord,w)` adds `2*w*delta`; native
fragment inverse `w=-.5` removes exactly delta. Previous phase derives from
`(frameCounter+720719)%720720` for independent raster SSR history. Main c2 is
stored on an unjittered output lattice and never adds previous jitter.

One center+eight-neighbor gather replaces the native current neighborhood.
Colors/depth0/depth1/materials are fetched once for those keys; no second native
neighborhood executes in the active branch. Neighbor inclusion requires matching
material and max normalized depth0/depth1 difference no greater than
`max(.0005,centerLinearDepth1*.01)`. Reconstruction uses separable tent weights
`max(0,1-|tap.x-key.x|)*max(0,1-|tap.y-key.y|)`, normalized over compatible taps;
zero weight falls back to center. Compatible colors form native ClipAABB bounds.
Native depth-edge and leaf smoothing treatment is carried into the new resolve;
this is a changed reconstruction algorithm, not demonstrated native AA identity.

Motion uses `p=Reproject(s,z_s)`, **`h=u-(s-p)`**. Static camera gives `h=u` for
every phase, rather than collapsing output pixels onto selected internal centers.
Same-surface X/Y neighbors already gathered supply a local plane: reciprocal
view depth is affine in projected UV. Current plane depth is evaluated at `u`
for stored c2 alpha; transformed previous plane depth is evaluated at **h**, not
p, normalized by metadata previous far. Degenerate/unfit plane rejects history.
Nearest previous alpha is compared with that expected depth. Frozen tolerance is
`2^-24 + abs(expected)*3/1024 + min(localDepthSpread*.25,.002)`; it covers FP16
alpha/previous-far quantization plus bounded current local variation. This is a
conservative model requiring actual driver/quality validation.

No history for native entity100–199/hand254 masks, hand-range depth, incompatible
transparent depth0/1 or cloud obstruction. Such output seeds current color and
writes alpha-1. Other rejected history also immediately seeds current; there is
no stale crossfade. Accepted history uses selected native5-tap Catmull or explicit
level0 bilinear choice, then ClipAABB. Native smoothing weight is reused. Fresh
sample confidence is `clamp(1-2*dot(key-center,key-center),0,1)`; history weight is
`min(.95,nativeWeight+(.95-nativeWeight)*(1-confidence)*.5)`. No parameter search.

Before any filtered RGB history read, all physical bilinear2 × 2 supports of all
five Catmull calls, or the single bilinear call, must remain in bounds and avoid
all eight metadata texels. Checking only nominal tap centers is insufficient.
Near the strip the output seeds current color. Metadata includes marker/version/
scale, exact output dimensions, exact frame chunks/medium, near/far/AA, world
clock/day/moon, weather/flash/eye/darkness and modulo64 clock/sun/preset. Vertex
checks sequence/reset/state; no fragment metadata loop. Pinned Iris1.8.12 jar
hash and `javap` bytecode receipt establish counter domain0..720719 and wrap720720.
All720720 low/mid base1024 tokens roundtrip FP16 exactly; high chunk is0.

Conservative guards reject >8 world-tick advance/rewind, day/moon change,
lightning change, medium change, >2 blocks/frame translation, projection scale
change >.0001, >.25 s modulo-clock advance, or nonfinite metadata. Ordinary
rain/wetness/eye/darkness changes use .002 absolute plus1/1024 relative tolerance;
near/far use only1/1024 relative. These exact choices are frozen, not a complete
proof of animated-object validity or environment continuity.

## Mechanism, benefit and intrinsic cost

The candidate interleaves native shadow support over alternate native TAA
frames. Ordinary **SOLID** terrain beyond `Far + Transition` (104 blocks at
32/96/8) evaluates one native symmetric shadow pair instead of two. It keeps
the original offset/radius denominator, selected pair coordinates, native
gradient noise, comparison/color sampling and shadow bias. Normalization is
adjusted to the retained pair. Near terrain, cutout/foliage, SSS, water, hand,
entities and other draw stages retain the original kernel. This is approximate
visibility, not exact shadow elimination. Two-frame response matches native
only with frozen inputs/gradient; actual jitter/light/caster changes prevent
claiming exact temporal equivalence.

For VL the candidate merges pairs of consecutive **native** integration
intervals wholly beyond the same protected boundary. It evaluates alternating
native endpoints using the unchanged `nearSamples` denominator. The interval
mass is `W(end2)-W(start)`. Unequal original interval weights are preserved by
RGB importance compensation: even phase uses `2*weight1/union`, odd phase
`2*weight2/union`. Thus the two-frame average equals the original weighted
response for frozen density/weights; alpha keeps union mass every frame. This
does not establish per-frame equality or stability during motion.

Both intervals must end strictly before the original ray-end break and at or
before native front-surface/entity depth. They must start beyond the protected
boundary, stay in the native near-sampling section, and have valid positive
weights. Underwater and non-unit translucency retain full native work. Far
section, ray-end/entity break semantics, native near counts/positions,
colored density/tint, feedback singleton and final color transforms stay live.
No old sample-budget denominator, spatial resolver, cache or field reuse is used.

**Expected total-frame benefit is an unmeasured low-single-digit hypothesis.**
The candidate removes two `SampleShadow` evaluations per eligible terrain
fragment and one complete VL density evaluation per eligible distant pair.
Actual coverage and GPU share are unknown. Historical whole terrain and
composite1 scope costs are sufficient for an early screen, not isolated saved
budget or evidence of 9%. The original elapsed/frame values remain
7.825/8.148 ms; reproducing 9% FPS would require net 0.646/0.673 ms savings.

Intrinsic overhead includes core/distance/stage/material predicates, the
temporal phase, three scalar weight evaluations and a divide for attempted VL
pairs, extra live values and wrappers. No new texture-based classifier,
render target, pass, history allocation or Java registration is added. This
overhead can outweigh saved sampling. Primary quality risk is temporally
varying distant shadow/shaft noise, colored visibility, importance-weight
brightness fluctuation, and popping as pairs enter the budget boundary. Native
TAA is retained without altered jitter/blend/sharpening; that does not prove it
conceals these changes. Moving foliage/casters, glass/shoreline boundaries and
distant thin shadow/shaft cues need inspection.

## Work avoided and exact output contract

The native positive-cloud-sample path is:

```glsl
if (shadowLength < lTracePos)
if (GetShadowOnCloud(...)) {
    if (eyeBrightness.y != 240) continue;
}
```

`GetShadowOnCloud` has no mutable output parameter/global write. It projects
the point into the shadow map and conditionally performs one native hardware
comparison lookup. When the Iris uniform `eyeBrightness.y == 240`, both
possible boolean results proceed to the identical native opacity/color/depth
work. Its result has exactly zero contribution in this condition.

The candidate computes a uniform eligibility boolean once before the cloud
marcher. It adds `&& !shaderlodCloudShadowElideR1` **before** the helper call.

projection/distance calculation and up to one comparison lookup. It adds no
texture-based classification, fetch or derivative. Remaining native query
calls keep their original coordinates and sampling expression. The new
eligibility condition uses only draw uniforms; it adds no nonuniform sampling
branch or changed implicit derivative requirement. The original sample-local
cloud and shadow branches remain upstream.

## Actual expression and exits

I read the original `shaders/lib/materials/materialMethods/reflections.glsl` and sequentially applied every maintained replacement for that member in memory; all 18 encountered anchors matched once. Native member SHA256 is `3b6d3b6477680a89ab56a2c0ae053b56b7b6b8cb39dabfba3d688772dac005ec`. Native `dist` starts at0, is assigned `length(start-rfragpos)` after each actual depth read/reconstruction, and has no recurrence or exit-condition read. Subsequent native loop operations read `err`, `vector`, `sr`, `tvector` and `viewPosRT`; they do not modify `start` or the last reconstructed `rfragpos` after that assignment.

The selected recipe suppresses only this overwritten assignment, records `shaderlodSampled=true`, and computes the identical expression after the loop when both metric and sampled are true. Consequently:

- No iterations, or clipping before the first depth sample: native and selected keep `dist=0`; the selected path does not invent a distance from initialized rfragpos.
- One or several samples, including all-zero reconstructed positions or empty depth1 samples: sampled means an actual source sample, not a nonzero/hit value. Both paths use the last reconstructed position, even if reflection is subsequently rejected.
- Clipping at the top of a later iteration: refPos can change before clipping; rfragpos remains the prior actual sample. Both distances therefore refer to that same prior sample.
- Crossing/refinement termination: rfragpos is already reconstructed and sampled is already recorded before native `sr>=refinementCount` break. The final selected distance matches that iteration's native distance.
- Natural exhaustion: post-loop viewPosRT updates do not change the saved rfragpos. Both use the final actual sample, not a projected unsampled endpoint.

For K actual sampled iterations, the source expression count becomes K→1 for K>=1 and remains0→0, bounded by native30 iterations on this default path. Native err/vector lengths remain paid. No ray, texture, refinement, sample-coordinate, normalization, AA or integration-count reduction follows.
